az_prescott_bouldering.blurb: Prescott Bouldering sits in central Arizona around the town of Prescott, at roughly 5,300 feet. It is almost entirely bouldering, with a lone gear line mixed in. Most problems are on the Groom Creek hillside just south of town, on granite with slopey holds. Copper Basin and the Thumb Butte loop add basalt boulders with pockets, while Granite Mountain, a set of in-town spots and several outlying areas fill out the rest. Grades start with a big crowd of V0 and easier problems, thin steadily through the middle grades, and reach a handful of hard lines near V10 and V11. Elevation changes between sites, so a day with poor weather elsewhere can still be workable here.

ca_yosemite_valley_bouldering.blurb: Yosemite Valley Bouldering is spread across Yosemite Valley in Yosemite National Park, in many separate boulder sectors. The rock is granite, and the problems lean toward technical slabs, crimpy faces, steep overhangs and a few highballs. Grades run from V0 up to the V12 range, with the biggest crowd between V0 and V5 and a long, thinning tail above. The biggest sectors include Curry Village, Housekeeping, the Ahwahnee Boulders and the Lower Yosemite Falls Boulders, and many smaller groups lie between them. Spring and fall are the comfortable seasons. Summer can be hot, though shade helps, and winter brings thinner crowds along with snow.

ct_eastern_highlands.blurb: Eastern Highlands gathers the climbing of eastern Connecticut, mostly in state parks and forests. Bouldering makes up the bulk, from V0 and below up to about V10, with most problems in the easier V1 to V4 range. Mashamoquet Brook State Park in Pomfret has quiet woodland approaches of 15 to 20 minutes and is at its best in early spring and fall. Hurd Park, near East Haddam, scatters its boulders along a loop trail, and rock quality there swings from excellent to sandy. Ross Rocks, near the Rhode Island line, offers cliffs of 30 to 90 feet with mostly top-roped and trad lines, some bolted routes, and stiffly graded climbing between about 5.5 and 5.12. Ice forms there in some winters.

co_buffalo_creek.blurb: Buffalo Creek is a South Platte granite area near the small settlement between Deckers and Pine, at about 7,000 feet. The climbing is mainly trad, with nearly as much bouldering and a small amount of sport. Expect a mix of good cracks, weaker cracks and runout slabs. Most roped routes fall between 5.8 and 5.11, with the largest share around 5.10, and boulder problems run from V0 to V12. Da Butts is a south-facing trad wall that can be pleasant on a warm winter day, while Top of the World is a remote scatter of small formations with one- to three-pitch routes. The Castle and a large bouldering sector round out the main areas. It is spread out, with many forest roads.

wa_shuksan_baker_neighbors.blurb: This region covers the western half of Whatcom County, around Bellingham and along the Mount Baker Highway. Bouldering is the largest part, followed by sport, then trad, top-rope, ice, mixed, alpine and mountaineering lines on the high peaks such as Mount Shuksan and Mount Baker. Near Bellingham, Chuckanut sandstone holds hundreds of problems in the trees of Larrabee State Park, with slabs, caves, huecos and steep faces, mostly V0 to V9. Wet sandstone is fragile, so give it time to dry. Roped climbing is mostly sport and trad, from about 5.9 to 5.12, with a few easier lines, and the Baker Crags are the main roped sub-area along the highway.

co_redgarden_wall.blurb: Redgarden Wall is the largest and tallest cliff in Eldorado Canyon State Park, south of Boulder, at about 6,000 feet. The rock is mostly firm, fine-grained sandstone, with short patches of weaker stone. Climbing is overwhelmingly trad: face climbing, cracks, dihedrals and roofs, often with sparse protection and tricky route-finding. Routes run roughly 30 to 600 feet and many are multi-pitch. Grades start near 5.5 and reach the low 5.13s, with most climbs between 5.9 and 5.12 and a big cluster around 5.11. Sections include the South Buttress, Tower One, Tower Two and the Roof Routes. Plan the descent before leaving the ground. Snow and ice linger on trails from mid-October to late April, and summer afternoons bring storms.
